alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 29 at 10:07PM MDT until October 1 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Animas
River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, Northwest San Juan
Mountains, Paradox Valley/Lower Dolores River, San Juan River
Basin, Southwest San Juan Mountains and Uncompahgre Plateau and
Dallas Divide and southeast Utah, including the following areas,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn scars, at low-water
crossings, and along creeks, streams, washes, arroyos and other
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Unpaved roads could become muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rainfall, associated with remnant moisture from
Hurricane Polo, are expected to produce numerous showers and
embedded thunderstorms. Heavy rain falling on saturated soils and
burn scars could lead to localized flash flooding and rises on
local rivers. Rainfall is expected to end by late Wednesday, but
rivers may rise out of their banks overnight Wednesday even after
rainfall has ended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

afd.snippet: 000 FXUS65 KGJT 301121 AFDGJT Area Forecast Discussion National Weather Service Grand Junction CO 521 AM MDT Wed Sep 30 2026 .KEY MESSAGES... - Scattered to widespread precipitation showers and storms continue through Wednesday evening. - Flooding concerns are increased for rain-soaked terrain, especially within and adjacent to the southern San Juans. - A Flood Watch is in effect for southeast Uta

fwf.snippet: .DISCUSSION...Moisture will continue to wrap into southern and central portions of the area today as this system moves through. Tropical moisture remains in place and moderate to heavy rain showers will continue to be a threat with high probability of wetting rainfall. Warmer and drier conditions move in by tomorrow and persist through the remainder of the forecast. Critical fire weather condition

alerts.title: US 160 Pagosa Springs Reconstruction-147581
alerts.description: Between US 84 and Pike Drive (Pagosa Springs) from Mile Point 144.3 to Mile Point 141.8. Road construction. Starting October 2, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until October 2, 2026 at about 6:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • October 2, 7:00AM - October 2, 6:00PM Comment: Harman Park & Piedra Road-Work is underway at this intersection of US 160. Working hours will be intermittent day and night so motorists should plan for potential delays, Monday-Saturday. Please allow extra time to get through the work zone. Safety benefits of this work includes pedestrian safety upgrades and ADA accessibility improvements. Expect lane shifts and up to 15-minute delays. Crews will switch two-way traffic into the eastbound lanes, perform temporary striping operations and begin asphalt milling in the westbound lanes. Parking will not be permitted on US 160 and vehicles will be towed at the owner's expense. Westbound lane closures, 10’ width and 75’ length restrictions will remain in place 24/7 through end of 2026. Work is weather-dependent. For questions contact the project team at 970-335-9230 or Pagosa160reconstruction@gmail.com Project Webpage: www.codot.gov/projects/us160pagosasprings
